standards.name: Minimum Information Required Guideline for Stroke Research and Clinical Data Reporting (Version 1.0)
standards.abstract: The guideline targets stroke research and clinical data reporting: it covers participant, study and experiment-level information collected in clinical and research settings (primarily clinical data captured in REDCap/ODM XML). The standard is a proposed reporting guideline developed by members of H3ABioNet/H3Africa to harmonise and standardise data collection, reporting and sharing for stroke research; it arose from consolidation of existing measures and reporting standards, was reviewed by domain researchers and clinicians, and is published with an associated REDCap XML schema to facilitate implementation.

classification.rationale: The published article presents prose guidance and reporting recommendations (a guideline) describing what to report, how elements are classified (participant-, study-, experiment-level; essential vs optional) and that an XML schema is supplied. Although an accompanying REDCap/ODM XML artifact exists, the journal article itself frames the output as reporting recommendations/checklist-style guidance rather than a fixed field-level data dictionary with explicit types in the text; therefore the source is best represented as PRINCIPLE.

principles.principle: Purpose: develop and propose a standardised reporting guideline for stroke research and clinical data reporting.
principles.evidence: "The current project aimed to develop and propose a standardised reporting guideline for stroke research and clinical data reporting."

principles.principle: Scope: reporting elements are organised as participant-, study- and experiment-level information.
principles.evidence: "Data elements within the reporting standard were classified as participant-, study- and experiment-level information, further subdivided into essential or optional information, and defined using existing ontologies."

principles.principle: Elements are further subdivided into essential or optional information.
principles.evidence: "Data elements within the reporting standard were classified as participant-, study- and experiment-level information, further subdivided into essential or optional information, and defined using existing ontologies."

principles.principle: Semantic standardisation: data elements are defined using existing ontologies to promote interoperability.
principles.evidence: "Data elements within the reporting standard were classified as participant-, study- and experiment-level information, further subdivided into essential or optional information, and defined using existing ontologies."

principles.principle: Development method: recommendations were consolidated from existing reporting standards and measures and reviewed by domain experts via an online survey.
principles.evidence: "Through systematic consolidation and harmonization of published data collection and reporting standards, several recommendations were drafted for the proposed guideline. These recommendations were reviewed by domain-researchers and clinicians using an online survey, developed in REDCap."

principles.principle: Implementation support: the guideline is accompanied by an XML schema for REDCap to ease data capture, sharing and governance.
principles.evidence: "It is accompanied with an associated XML schema for REDCap implementation, to increase the user friendliness of data capturing, sharing, reporting and governance."

principles.principle: Intended users and adaptability: the reporting guideline can be used for research utility and adapted for clinical utility; intended users include clinicians, healthcare workers, researchers, data managers and bioinformaticians.
principles.evidence: "The proposed reporting guideline can be employed for research utility and adapted for clinical utility as well."

principles.principle: Intended users (explicit in REDCap metadata): "To be employed by clinicians, healthcare workers, researchers, data managers and bioinformaticians."
principles.evidence: "<redcap:PurposeOther>To be employed by clinicians, healthcare workers, researchers, data managers and bioinformaticians.</redcap:PurposeOther>"

standards.notes: Source materials include a research-article describing the guideline (Data Science Journal) and an accompanying REDCap/ODM XML export containing the actual field names and form structure. The article frames the output as reporting recommendations and classification guidance; the full XML (ODM) artifact provides a deployable form definition but the journal text primarily presents principle-style guidance.
